Cautious but policy-backstopped. The FOMC highlights pandemic-driven downside risks and a moderated recovery, offset by strong accommodation (0–1/4 percent policy rate, ongoing Treasury and agency MBS purchases, and outcome-based guidance). SLOOS evidence is mixed but slightly improving at the margin: banks still cite the economic outlook, industry-specific problems, and risk tolerance as constraints, yet large banks eased standards for several mortgage categories; foreign banks reported strengthened C&I loan demand; and small banks expect stronger consumer-loan demand with some easing tied to better credit quality, even as some portfolios still prompt tightening. These SLOOS signals modestly temper the downside tone but leave conditions risk-aware. Net tone: cautious with credible backstops and an uneven thaw in lending.
